summary: Phase 149O.20L.7A -- Class-B Dell Target Re-Selection & Read-Only Preflight. PLANNING/PREFLIGHT phase, read-only against the Dell, no provisioning, no CHGR published. Performed the first legitimate, read-only SSH connection to the Dell (hac-dell, 192.168.192.200) using an already-existing codex account/key (loaded into the operator's own ssh-agent by the operator, passphrase never seen or handled by this phase) -- no account, group, key, or sudoers entry was created. Confirmed live host identity independent of hostname/IP: Dell Inc. Latitude E5470, hostname atila-Latitude-E5470, machine-id 54ff22ce400b475aa0d55cb68f4a3334, Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-28-generic, amd64. Confirmed operator account codex holds unrestricted passwordless sudo. Enumerated existing principals (atila uid 1000, uosserver uid 1001, codex uid 1003, clawdbot uid 995) -- no pcae/pcae-deploy name collision; all home directories mode 0750, confirmed isolated. Re-derived L.5A's twelve target-eligibility criteria for Linux/Ubuntu against this host: verdict ELIGIBLE WITH PRECONDITIONS (python3-venv/python3-pip must be apt-installed before venv creation, since system pip/ensurepip are absent and the interpreter is PEP-668 externally-managed; no other blocker found -- ancestor chain for /, /etc, /opt already root-owned mode 0755 with no ACL entries; getfacl/setfacl functional; /usr/bin/git root-owned trusted). Selected Model 1 deployment-principal architecture: a single new dedicated pcae agent identity (nologin, no SSH login surface), with admin write-authority over Protected Root and other authority-bearing state exercised via the existing codex sudo channel rather than a second persistent admin OS account -- reasoned against HBDC-001 section 7's exactly-two-distinct-principals requirement and section 9's own 'combined human-approver/bootstrap-admin role in v1' framing; Model 2 (a second pcae-deploy identity) was rejected for lacking any identified authority/security benefit beyond what the operator's own sudo channel already provides. Froze exact literal names/paths for the next phase's proposition: pcae principal/group; Protected Root /etc/pcae/hatp/trust-store (root:pcae, 0750 -- fixed by the existing hatp_bootstrap.py platform-keyed resolver, not a choice made this phase); PCAE runtime install /opt/pcae/runtime (root:pcae, 0750); per-repository workspaces /opt/pcae/projects/<slug>/repo (pcae:pcae, 0750, rw); non-repo-scoped state /var/lib/pcae and logs /var/log/pcae (root:pcae, 0750). Preserved the per-repository consumption model unchanged (PCAE governance state remains inside each governed repository's own .pcae/ directory, as today; a shared runtime install is a deployment convenience, not a step toward centralized multi-repository governance, which remains explicitly deferred and out of scope). Confirmed via source inspection (src/pcae/core/hatp_class_b_conformance.py, hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py, hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py) that verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() has no remote/host abstraction -- it only inspects the local calling process's own euid/environment/filesystem state, and cannot evaluate the Dell by being invoked from the Mac. It was not run live against the Dell this phase, since doing so would require placing PCAE source on the target's filesystem, which this phase's own boundary explicitly defers to a future provisioning phase; this is disclosed as an expected pre-provisioning absence classified as a deployment concern, not a product implementation gap, and no live COMPLIANT/NON_COMPLIANT result is fabricated. Produced a reasoned (not measured) HBDC failure-family inventory from the live read-only findings, mapping every row to 'observation only' or 'authorized future mutation,' none to 'unsupported implementation gap.' Derived a literal nine-action Ubuntu provisioning plan (apt package install; pcae group/principal creation; Protected Root creation; runtime/state directory tree creation; home directory normalization; pinned-commit source clone; venv creation and editable install; launch-wrapper creation; final read-only verifier confirmation), each with exact command, privilege requirement, precondition, expected mutation, read-back command, rollback command, and rollback verification -- and explained why the action count coincidentally matches the Mac plan's own nine despite materially different composition (an added apt-package precondition step not needed on macOS, offset by collapsing the Mac plan's separate ACL-configuration and three-way PYTHONPATH/sitecustomize/git-PATH lockdown steps into single steps, since this Dell's default POSIX permissions and a from-scratch launch wrapper already satisfy those requirements without separate interventions). Defined idempotency and failure/rollback-order semantics for the full action graph. Drafted (but did not publish) a complete, literal Dell-specific Boundary-P proposition, explicitly labeled DRAFT -- NOT AUTHORIZED, containing exact host identity, principal/group names, paths, source binding, contracts, action graph, privileged operations, rollback semantics, exclusions, and migration implications, with no placeholder remaining. No pcae decision-session was started and no CHGR was published this phase. The existing Mac CHGR (chgr-d4343fa51b9743f3abaeb87a881a78b1) was independently re-inspected (still published/approved, decision_subject still names the Mac specifically, no revocation/supersession field) but neither modified nor reused as authority for the Dell. Boundary P remains NOT AUTHORIZED (Dell-specific proposition ready for human election); Boundary C and Boundary A remain explicitly NOT AUTHORIZED; Class-B remains NOT PROVISIONED; HATP remains NOT READY; runtime unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable). Developer environment (atilamadai account, ~/repos/pcae-harness checkout) confirmed unchanged; git status --short clean throughout except this phase's own documented artifacts. New, independently authored companion test module -- 26 tests, re-run three consecutive times, 26 passed each run, no flake; asserts documentary/planning content and continued absence of any Dell-provisioning or CHGR-publication artifact, without performing live Dell SSH within routine pytest execution. Recommends exactly one next phase: 149O.20L.7B -- Dell Class-B Boundary-P Authorization Record Capture, which must present the complete literal proposition to the human and capture a fresh APPROVE/DECLINE/AMEND election before any real Dell mutation may be authorized. Not begun by this phase.
